Underwriters do the filtering. A seat needs an errors-and-omissions policy from a carrier on the state insurance register: the applicant files twelve months of operating history, names a principal, pays for a site inspection, and the node reads the register monthly for lapse or unpaid premium.

Fifty clones carry fifty premiums near 1,200 dollars a year on a 50,000 dollar limit, 60,000 dollars gone with no claim filed. A ferry punches one ticket per passenger, so the underwriter prices one hull per name, and nobody quotes a pearl voyage policy against an empty quay and an unlit lantern.
